source.title: Bipartite invariance in mouse primary visual cortex
source.authors: Zhi-Wei Ding; D. Tran; Kayla Ponder; Zhuo-Kun Ding; R. Froebe; Lydia Ntanavara; Paul G. Fahey; Erick Cobos; L. Baroni; Maria Diamantaki; Eric Y. Wang; Andersen Chang; S. Papadopoulos; Jia-Kun Fu; Taliah Muhammad; Christos Papadopoulos; Santiago A. Cadena; Alexandros Evangelou; K. Willeke; Fabio Anselmi; Sophia Sanborn; J. Antolík; Emmanouil Froudarakis; Saumil S. Patel; Edgar Y. Walker; J. Reimer; Fabian H Sinz; Alexander S. Ecker; Katrin Franke; X. Pitkow; A. Tolias

record.tranche_reason: The study measures stimulus invariance in mouse V1 neurons, not polysemanticity in trained artificial networks described by the claim versions. It cites related work on artificial neurons but does not test the AI-model claims.
record.gate_note: The reported findings concern biological mouse V1 neurons and their responses to synthesized stimuli. They do not measure AI neurons in image classifiers or language models; therefore no claim version is tested. The paper also cites prior ANN work on texture cells and high-low frequency detectors, but those cited results are not this study’s findings.
record.test_reason: The study characterises invariance (selectivity plus tolerated variation) of biological mouse V1 L2/3 neurons via a CNN digital twin and in vivo verification. It measures no polysemanticity in trained artificial networks: no units responding to unrelated inputs, no superposition, architecture or measurement-dependence tests. The ANN work it mentions (texture cells, high-low frequency detectors) is only cited. 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses', since the paper never discusses polysemanticity itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that mouse V1 neurons show a spectrum of invariance, including a novel bipartite invariance (one fixed subfield, one phase-invariant texture subfield). Its division aligns with spatial-frequency-defined object boundaries, suggesting a role in texture-based segmentation. They also report replicating bipartite DEIs in the MICrONS data set.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses deep predictive models and diverse exciting inputs to characterize biological mouse V1; it does not reproduce the original AI-neuron claim’s measurement or test a listed AI-model version.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report similar DEI results across pixel-space versus population-response diversity measures and across predictive-model/stimulus-domain variants; no listed AI-neuron measurement was performed.

fits_no_version.finding: Mouse V1 neurons span a continuum of phase invariance, and many show bipartite receptive fields: one subfield is fixed, the other is phase-invariant and texture-like.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Biological V1 neurons can show bipartite phase invariance across receptive-field subfields.

fits_no_version.finding: Modeled mouse V1 neurons prefer texture-defined boundaries with spatial-frequency differences, resembling high-low frequency detectors described in ANNs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Biological V1 neurons act like ANN high-low frequency detectors, preferring frequency-defined object boundaries.

record.problems: The study concerns biological mouse V1 rather than AI networks. The authors state that sample sizes were not predetermined statistically and that data collection and analysis were not blind to conditions. Some closed-loop analyses selected neurons with relatively high invariance, although they report supplementary verification on randomly selected populations.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted supporting stimulus-control and subfield-swap outcomes, additional model-variant comparisons, and further supplemental analyses because they concern validation of the biological DEI method rather than any listed AI-model claim version.

untested.parts: No artificial image-classifier units are examined for responses to unrelated inputs.
No tests of initialization, regularization or noise.
No architecture or activation-function comparison of polysemanticity.
No reanalysis of canonical polysemantic AI neurons.
No test of how polysemanticity depends on activation range or scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The only link to the claim is citing the Distill circuits-thread work on high-low frequency detectors and ANN texture cells. The study contributes no evidence on polysemantic neurons in artificial networks.

versions.untested_parts: Artificial image-classifier neurons; no AI network units are measured for responses to unrelated image inputs.
No language models, MLP neurons, tokens, or language contexts.
No test of superposition, feature-to-neuron capacity pressure, or sparse feature packing in artificial networks.
No test of artificial-network initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity.
No comparison of AI architectures or activation functions, no SoLU test, and no assessment of AI performance costs.
The paper studies biological receptive-field subfields, not whether canonical polysemantic units in AI networks share a feature or related job.
No test of how AI-neuron polysemanticity changes with activation range or explanation-scoring method.

rows.subject: mouse V1 neurons (6464 model V1 neurons)
rows.size_stated: 6464 model V1 neurons; 617 tested in closed-loop experiments
rows.operation_detail: Measured diversity of optimized Diverse Exciting Inputs (DEIs) using normalized pairwise pixel-space distances.

conditions.value: DEIs optimized to activate target neurons

rows.baseline: Simulated simple-cell and complex-cell reference values
rows.value: Mouse V1 diversity indexes spanned a continuous spectrum, with simulated simple and complex cells at the two extremes.
rows.note: This is a finding about biological mouse V1 neurons, not artificial network neurons.
rows.check: Biological neurons' DEI diversity index measures invariance, not polysemanticity. The 6464 neurons are model-predicted mouse V1 neurons (CNN digital twin), not units of a trained classifier.

rows.subject: mouse V1 neurons (500 neurons pooled across 8 mice)
rows.operation_detail: Presented synthesized DEIs and MEIs to animals and compared target-neuron responses.

conditions.value: 20 repeats of MEI; 20 different DEIs with single repeat each

rows.measure: Normalized target-neuron response to DEIs relative to MEI
rows.value: DEIs achieved 75% of corresponding MEI activation in vivo; model prediction was 85%.
rows.uncertainty: Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, W = 51360, P = 4.92 × 10⁻⁴; 12.8% of neurons differed from 85% of MEI at P < 0.05.
rows.note: The result validates diverse activation-preserving stimuli for biological neurons.
rows.check: This is an in vivo validation of the DEI method (75% vs 85% of MEI), not a finding about any claim version. The Wilcoxon P concerns the in silico vs in vivo difference.

rows.subject: mouse V1 neurons (401 neurons pooled over 8 mice)
rows.operation_detail: Compared responses to non-parametric DEIs, full-texture DEIs, and partial-texture DEIs.

conditions.value: Full-field texture model (DEIsfull) versus non-parametric DEIs

rows.value: 52.9% of neurons showed significantly lower responses to DEIsfull.
rows.uncertainty: One-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, W = 4389, P < 10⁻⁹; individual-neuron comparison P < 0.05, one-tailed Welch’s t-test.
rows.note: The authors say a homogeneous full-field phase-invariance model failed to account for many neurons.
rows.check: This compares the study's own stimulus models (full-texture vs non-parametric DEIs). It is method comparison, unrelated to the versions. 'partial' as a state is not meaningful here.

rows.subject: mouse V1 neurons (401 neurons pooled over 8 mice)
rows.operation_detail: Compared responses to partial-texture DEIs and non-parametric DEIs.

conditions.value: Partial-texture model with fixed and phase-invariant subfields

rows.value: Partial-texture DEIs activated neurons similarly; only 8.7% showed significantly different responses.
rows.uncertainty: Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, W = 32429, P = 7.01 × 10⁻⁴; individual-neuron comparison P < 0.05, two-tailed Welch’s t-test.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as support for a biological receptive-field model with distinct fixed and phase-invariant subfields.
rows.check: This compares the study's own stimulus models. It is method validation on biological neurons.

rows.subject: mouse V1 neurons (1200 neurons pooled over 6 mice)
rows.operation_detail: Screened synthesized CUB-grating images with different boundary and spatial-frequency conditions using the predictive model.

conditions.value: Different spatial frequencies, identical spatial frequencies, or homogeneous gratings

rows.measure: Share of neurons most activated by each image condition
rows.value: 71.08% preferred heterogeneous crops with frequency differences; 28.58% preferred crops with identical frequency; 0.34% preferred homogeneous signals.
rows.uncertainty: One-way chi-squared test, χ² = 913.2, P < 10⁻⁹; bootstrapping P < 10⁻⁹ for both comparisons; error bars were bootstrapped STD.
rows.note: This is a result about biological neurons’ modeled responses to boundary stimuli.
rows.check: In silico screening of predicted biological-neuron responses. It is unrelated to AI-neuron polysemanticity.

rows.subject: mouse V1 neurons (1200 neurons pooled over 6 mice)
rows.operation_detail: Compared segmentation labels in highly activating natural-image crops with receptive-field subfield masks.

conditions.value: 100 highly activating and 100 random crops per neuron

rows.measure: Matching score between object segmentation and phase-invariant/fixed receptive-field subfields
rows.baseline: Random natural crops were not significantly aligned
rows.value: Highly activating crops had positive median matching scores; 59.25% of neurons showed greater matching to highly activating crops than to random crops.
rows.uncertainty: One-tailed one-sample t-test, t = 21.4, P < 10⁻⁹; comparison with random crops, W = 597254, P < 10⁻⁹.
rows.note: The paper relates the biological subfield division to object boundaries in natural images.
rows.check: Alignment of the subfield mask with object boundaries in biological-neuron models. It is unrelated to the versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
